title: Joint Minimax Risk for Optimal Value with Growing Treatment Menus and Sparse Groups
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered tier=subfield below floor=field; exact 2<K<d^2 frontier, instantiated certificate, matching estimator/converse, and general consistency boundary remain open.
gap_reasons: The note proves the full-class upper bound C min{1,dK log(eK)/n} and the lower bound c min{1,dK log(1+sqrt(K/d))/n}, which match only in the region K>=d^2; the exact frontier for 2<K<d^2, the advertised attaining estimator, and the consistency boundary remain open.
The missing central transition, absence of an instantiated certificate, and stale headline claims prevent a field-tier paper.
proof_attempt_summary: The run verified a computable full-class upper bound and centered-winner lower bound, matching them for K>=d^2, and discharged the one-group and parametric-boundary results. It then tested whether a dimension-uniform polynomial/factorial certificate could close 2<K<d^2, but the proposed salvage supplied no candidate rate, coefficient construction, variance control, or matching normalized priors. The exact central frontier, attaining all-regime estimator/converse, and general consistency boundary therefore remain open.
tldr: A growing treatment menu turns each sparse patient group into a high-dimensional nonsmooth maximum with random denominators. The headline kernel is the explicit all-regime minimax MSE \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), with a total statistically computable estimator on the full unknown-mass class under menu-scaled lower overlap alone and a matching same-class converse. The mathematical hinge is a dimension-uniform certificate that makes maximum-approximation bias, exact factorial-lift covariance, and normalized moment-prior mixture geometry share one evaluated scale, while exposing the finite coefficient count \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\) and the estimator's combinatorial evaluation cost. Supporting claims cover the one-group and \(K\ge d^2\) rates and a new binary-to-many-arm hardness transfer; the accepted \(K=2\) frontier is used only as a cited boundary condition. The open content is the exact transition for \(2<K<d^2\) and the resulting necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary.
gap: The literature separates fixed-dimensional nonregular inference, restricted-class policy regret, one-group maximum-mean upper bounds, and scalar approximation-theoretic minimax estimation; none gives the joint finite-sample risk when sparse categorical groups and treatments grow together under unknown observational logging and only a menu-scaled lower propensity bound.
fill: The project evaluates that certificate, splices it to the supporting one-group and many-arm results, the new binary-grouping transfer, and the cited \(K=2\) boundary, then turns the closed-form envelope into a total computable estimator, an all-estimator lower bound, and exact consistency and parametric-MSE conditions.
